language.script: Latin (æ, ø, å — same letter set as Norwegian, differing spelling/vocabulary)

terrainDescription.zh: 地形極為平坦，全國無真正山脈，以農業平原與眾多島嶼、綿長海岸線為主要特徵，與挪威、瑞典的多山地形形成明顯對比。
terrainDescription.en: Exceptionally flat with no real mountains anywhere in the country — dominated by agricultural plains, numerous islands, and a long coastline, in clear contrast to mountainous Norway and Sweden.

plate.color: white background, black text (standard private cars); other colors by vehicle type; blue EU band with "DK" — Denmark was the last EU country to adopt the EU-format plate, in 2009

roadInfra.bollardStyle: A highly distinctive white bollard with a yellow reflector and a dark orange stripe, found on almost every road — one of the most reliable single-country bollard clues in Europe; outer road lines made of small white squares are another distinctive Danish marking

utilityPole.transformerMount: Standard street-level utility poles are actually rare in Denmark; rural electricity infrastructure instead relies on large, towering overhead transmission lines, often running near highways — their absence/scale is itself the identifying clue rather than a specific pole style

historicalContext.zh: 丹麥語與挪威語共用 æ、ø、å 字母，但拼字與詞彙仍有差異；丹麥全境地勢平坦、無高山，這點與地形崎嶇的挪威、瑞典形成強烈對比；丹麥也是最後一個採用歐盟式車牌設計的歐盟成員國（2009年）。
historicalContext.en: Danish shares the æ/ø/å letters with Norwegian, though spelling and vocabulary still differ. Denmark's famously flat, mountain-free terrain contrasts sharply with rugged Norway and Sweden. Denmark was also the last EU member state to adopt the EU-format license plate, in 2009.
